plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A widely cultivated perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives in the cooling days of autumn because it flowers in response to shortening day length.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and the flower is the emblem of the Japanese Imperial family and the subject of Japan's annual Chrysanthemum Festival.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, hardy native wildflower with clusters of daisy-like blooms with golden-yellow centers. It is a late-season nectar source for pollinators and thrives in meadows, roadsides, and wet prairies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Quebec to Alabama and west to the Rockies
plants.funFact: New England Asters are a critical late-season food source for migrating monarch butterflies as they travel south to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the leaves fully emerge. In spring, entire streets and parks turn violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and Brazil
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, around 70,000 trees bloom each October, and in Australia the flowering is traditionally linked to university exam season.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up bare stems topped with sparkling, wavy-petaled pink flowers in autumn, after its strap-like leaves have largely died back. It prefers warm, sunny, well-drained spots.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape and Drakensberg region; cultivated in gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The petals have a shimmering, glittery look caused by specialized surface cells that sparkle in sunlight, which is why it is sometimes called the diamond lily.
